:::{#thm-power-product}
#### Power of a product

If $a, b > 0$ and $c \in \reals$, then

$$(ab)^c = a^c \cd b^c$$

When $c$ is a positive integer,
the same identity holds for all $a, b \in \reals$,
because both sides are products of $c$ copies of $a$ and $c$ copies of $b$,
which can be regrouped by @thm-prod-symmetric and @thm-prod-assoc.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-power-product}
#### Power of a product

With $a = 2$, $b = 3$, and $c = 2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
(2 \cd 3)^2 &= 6^2 \\
&= 36,
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
2^2 \cd 3^2 &= 4 \cd 9 \\
&= 36.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
